notice: Easy Mode dramatically simplifies the process of filter selection. Select between Playlist (a mix of content quality and sources back-to-back) or Album modes (consistent production and quality), then pick your preset and its emphasis or version. Only a few of HQPlayer's filters are accessible here, so think of this like training wheels and don't be afraid to experiment.

help.body:
Choose 'Transients' for most multi-track studio recordings; these often have an artificial sense of space at best, but carry strong transient content like percussion.

Choose 'Space' for live or acoustic performances where the room or venue is part of the recording.

Note that the effect of these levers varies from preset to preset: for example, 'The Purist' adjusts the filter's length to change the emphasis; Old School, on the other hand, changes its phase.

'Hi-Res' modes are optimized for material with a sampling rate >=88.2 kHz, NOT any 24-bit content. These modes also work for lossy material like MQAs and MP3s.

The glyphs (A) and (1/2) indicate the error correction level (apodizing); if no or half error correction sounds harsh or generates an apodizing events warning, try a different setting.

Still can't decide? Experiment! Presets can be changed live at any time with only a brief interruption to playback.
